newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian tobacco tycoon Sampoerna buys into Astra.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian tobacco tycoon Sampoerna buys into Astra.

text.p: Indonesian tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna said on Monday that he had bought 9.81 percent of Astra International for 435.88 billion rupiah (US$189.51 million).
The purchase makes him the second-largest shareholder in the country's biggest vehicle-maker, which has been dogged by rumours of a takeover bid for the past two weeks.

Sampoerna, who controls cigarette company Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna and is one of the wealthiest men in the country, said in a letter to stock market watchdog Bapepam that he and his son Jonathan Sampoerna had bought the stake in Astra through several purchases on both the local and foreign board.
Copies of the letter were given to the press by Bapepam.
Sampoerna said in the letter that he bought 4.62 percent of the company, or about 53.6 million shares, from June to September 19 at a cost of about 161.6 billion rupiah.
On September 23 and 24, Sampoerna said he bought another 5.19 percent at a cost of 274.28 billion rupiah.
He did not specify if the shares were bought in block deals or through picking up floating stock. He also did not name any sellers.
Astra shares closed at 3,800 rupiah, up 25, on Monday. It closed at 2,625 on September 16.
Brokers said the fact that Sampoerna was one of the buyers of Astra was already known and that they were awaiting disclosures on other bidders.

An Indonesian newspaper has said members of President Suharto's family were also interested in building up stakes in Astra. It named his eldest daughter, Siti Hardianti Rukmana, and his sons Bambang Trihatmodjo and Hutomo Mandala Putra as prospective buyers.

The Bisnis Indonesia daily has said Rukmana, who controls toll-road operator Citra Marga, is in talks with timber magnate Prajogo Pangestu, Astra's largest shareholder, to buy out his 10.68 percent stake.
It has also said Sampoerna may sell his holdings to a group controlled by another timber tycoon Bob Hasan.
Neither report has been independently confirmed, but Bapepam said on Monday that Pangestu still held his original stake.
Hasan's Nusamba group is owned 80 percent by three foundations controlled by Suharto himself. The president's eldest son Sigit Hardjojudanto and Hasan hold 10 percent each.
Brokers have said buying a stake in Astra would be beneficial to both Trihatmodjo and Mandala Putra, who own separate joint ventures with South Korean vehicle manufacturers.

Mandala Putra is the sole beneficiary of Indonesia's controversial national car policy, which grants his company tax and tariff breaks subject to meeting local content requirements within three years.

Brokers say Astra's production and distribution base would be useful for either. They also see potential for synergy with Rukmana's toll-road operations as Astra is likely to bid for contracts to build Jakarta's elevated suburban train system.
Astra's holdings are widely held. After Pangestu and Sampoerna, the next largest chunk of shares is held by Japan's Toyota Motor Corp with 8.26 percent.
Brokers have said a holding of 18 percent to 20 percent can effectively control the company.
(US$1 = 2,300 rupiah)
